question: Could priests and bishops marry?

answers.label: Married men could be ordained and keep their wives
Married clergy must live in continence

overview.text: The apostles included married men: Clement of Alexandria notes Peter and Philip had children. At Nicaea, as Socrates tells it, Paphnutius stopped a law separating clergy from their wives.

In the Latin West, councils from about 306 required married bishops, priests and deacons to abstain from their wives, claiming apostolic custom. Pope Siricius in 385 bound priests and levites to continence from the day of their ordination.

In 1139 the Second Lateran Council went further: marriages contracted by clergy in major orders were declared no marriage at all. The Augsburg Confession (1530) replied that priests in the ancient Church were married men, and that a bishop should be the husband of one wife.

quotes.author: Clement of Alexandria
quotes.english: Peter and Philip had children, and Philip gave his daughters in marriage. And Paul does not hesitate in one letter to speak of his wife, whom he did not take around with him for the sake of his ministry's freedom.
quotes.original: Πέτρος μὲν γὰρ καὶ Φίλιππος ἐπαιδοποιήσαντο, Φίλιππος δὲ καὶ τὰς θυγατέρας ἀνδράσιν ἐξέδωκεν, καὶ ὅ γε Παῦλος οὐκ ὀκνεῖ ἔν τινι ἐπιστολῇ τὴν αὑτοῦ προσαγορεύειν σύζυγον, ἣν οὐ περιεκόμιζεν διὰ τὸ τῆς ὑπηρεσίας εὐσταλές.
quotes.context: Written against teachers who condemned marriage. The "wife" of Paul is Clement's reading of Philippians 4:3.

quotes.author: Council of Elvira
quotes.english: It was decided to forbid entirely bishops, presbyters and deacons, or all clerics serving in the ministry, to have relations with their wives and beget children. Whoever does so shall be removed from clerical office.
quotes.original: Placuit in totum prohibere episcopis, presbyteris et diaconibus, vel omnibus clericis positis in ministerio, abstinere se a coniugibus suis et non generare filios : quicumque vero fecerit, ab honore clericatus exterminetur.
quotes.context: The Latin is famously awkward: read literally it forbids them "to abstain". It is taken as a rule of continence for married clergy in Spain.

source.edition: Denzinger, Enchiridion symbolorum, 11th ed. (1911), Council of Elvira, canon 33

quotes.author: Paphnutius at Nicaea (as Socrates reports)
quotes.english: The bishops wanted to bring a new law into the Church, that those in holy orders, bishops, presbyters and deacons, should not sleep with the wives they had married while still laymen. When this was being discussed, Paphnutius stood up in the middle of the assembly of bishops and cried out not to lay a heavy yoke on the clergy, saying that marriage itself is honorable and the bed undefiled (Hebrews 13:4) ... that it was enough for those already ordained not to marry afterward, according to the Church's ancient tradition, but not to be separated from the wife they had once married as laymen.
quotes.original: Ἐδόκει τοῖς ἐπισκόποις νόμον νεαρὸν εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν εἰσφέρειν, ὥστε τοὺς ἱερωμένους, λέγω δὲ ἐπισκόπους καὶ πρεσβυτέρους καὶ διακόνους, μὴ συγκαθεύδειν ταῖς γαμεταῖς, ἃς ἔτι λαϊκοὶ ὄντες ἠγάγοντο. Καὶ ἐπεὶ περὶ τούτου βουλεύεσθαι προὔκειτο, διαναστὰς ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ συλλόγου τῶν ἐπισκόπων ὁ Παφνούτιος ἐβόα μακρὰ, μὴ βαρὺν ζυγὸν ἐπιθεῖναι τοῖς ἱερωμένοις ἀνδράσι, τίμιον εἶναι τὸν γάμον αὐτὸν καὶ τὴν κοίτην ἀμίαντον ... ἀρκεῖσθαι τε τὸν φθάσαντα κλήρου τυχεῖν μηκέτι ἐπὶ γάμον ἔρχεσθαι, κατὰ τὴν τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἀρχαίαν παράδοσιν, μὴ μὴν ἀποζεύγνυσθαι ταύτης, ἣν ἅπαξ ἤδη πρότερον λαϊκὸς ὢν ἠγάγετο.
quotes.context: Socrates writes a century later; some historians doubt the story. It matches the later Eastern rule: married men may be ordained, but no one marries after ordination.

quotes.author: Siricius
quotes.english: We have learned that very many priests of Christ and levites, long after their consecration, have fathered children both from their own wives and even from shameful intercourse. ... By these decrees all of us, priests and levites, are bound by an unbreakable law, so that from the day of our ordination we devote both our hearts and our bodies to sobriety and chastity. ... Any bishop, presbyter or deacon who is hereafter found to be such a man, which we do not desire, must understand that every way to pardon through us is now shut to him.
quotes.original: Plurimos enim sacerdotes Christi atque levitas, post longa consecrationis suae tempora, tam de coniugibus propriis, quam etiam de turpi coitu sobolem didicimus procreasse ... Quarum sanctionum omnes sacerdotes atque levitae insolubili lege constringimur, ut a die ordinationis nostrae, sobrietati ac pudicitiae et corda nostra mancipemus et corpora ... quilibet episcopus, presbyter atque diaconus, quod non optamus, deinceps fuerit talis inventus, iam nunc sibi omnem per nos indulgentiae aditum intelligat obseratum
quotes.context: Pope Siricius to Himerius of Tarragona (10 February 385), the first papal decretal on the subject: he treats clerical continence as a rule already in force, and Denzinger’s own note says the same. Levites here are deacons. Read from the scan of Denzinger’s Enchiridion (11th ed., 1911), no. 89, whose OCR is poor in places; the words quoted follow the standard text. No locked Siricius text exists in the library.

source.edition: Denzinger, Enchiridion symbolorum, 11th ed. (1911), Siricius, Letter to Himerius, 7 (no. 89)

quotes.author: Council of Carthage
quotes.english: Bishop Aurelius said: ... it was decided that the holy bishops and priests of God, and also the deacons, who serve the divine sacraments, should be continent in all things, so that they may obtain simply what they ask of the Lord; so that what the apostles taught and antiquity itself kept, we too may keep. ... All the bishops said: It is agreed that chastity be kept in all things and by all who serve the altar.
quotes.original: ita placuit, ut condecet, sacros antistites ac Dei sacerdotes, nec non et levitas, vel qui sacramentis divinis inserviunt, continentes esse in omnibus, quo possint simpliciter quod a Domino postulant impetrare, ut quod apostoli docuerunt, et ipsa servavit antiquitas, nos quoque custodiamus. ... Ab universis episcopis dictum est: Placet, ut in omnibus et ab omnibus pudicitia custodiatur qui altari inserviunt.
quotes.context: The African church claimed apostolic origin for clerical continence.

quotes.author: Council in Trullo
quotes.english: Since we know it to be handed down as a rule of the Roman Church that those who are deemed worthy to be advanced to the diaconate or presbyterate should promise no longer to cohabit with their wives, we, preserving the ancient rule and apostolic perfection and order, will that the lawful marriages of men who are in holy orders be from this time forward firm, by no means dissolving their union with their wives nor depriving them of their mutual intercourse at a convenient time. ... if anyone shall have been found worthy to be ordained subdeacon, or deacon, or presbyter, he is by no means to be prohibited from admittance to such a rank, even if he shall live with a lawful wife.
quotes.original: Since we know it to be handed down as a rule of the Roman Church that those who are deemed worthy to be advanced to the diaconate or presbyterate should promise no longer to cohabit with their wives, we, preserving the ancient rule and apostolic perfection and order, will that the lawful marriages of men who are in holy orders be from this time forward firm, by no means dissolving their union with their wives nor depriving them of their mutual intercourse at a convenient time. ... if anyone shall have been found worthy to be ordained subdeacon, or deacon, or presbyter, he is by no means to be prohibited from admittance to such a rank, even if he shall live with a lawful wife.
quotes.context: The Eastern council of 692 knew Rome's custom of separating clergy from their wives and refused it, ordering that the marriages of men in holy orders stand firm. Quoted here in Percival's standard English translation; the council's Greek text is still to be quoted when a lawful open Greek edition is secured.

source.edition: The Canons of the Council in Trullo, translated by H. R. Percival, in Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, 2nd series, vol. 14

quotes.author: Second Lateran Council
quotes.english: Following in the footsteps of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs Gregory VII, Urban and Paschal, we command that no one hear the Masses of those whom he knows to have wives or concubines. And so that the law of continence and the purity pleasing to God may spread among ecclesiastical persons and sacred orders, we decree that bishops, priests, deacons, subdeacons, canons regular, monks and professed lay brothers who, transgressing the holy resolve, have presumed to take wives to themselves, be separated. For we judge that a union of this kind, which is known to have been contracted against the Church’s rule, is not a marriage.
quotes.original: Ad haec praedecessorum nostrorum Gregorii VII, Urbani et Paschalis Romanorum pontificum vestigiis inhaerentes, praecipimus ut nullus missas eorum audiat, quos uxores vel concubinas habere cognoverit. Ut autem lex continentiae et Deo placens munditia in ecclesiasticis personis et sacris ordinibus dilatetur, statuimus quatenus episcopi presbyteri diaconi subdiaconi regulares canonici et monachi atque conversi professi, qui sanctum transgredientes propositum uxores sibi copulare praesumpserint, separentur. Huiusmodi namque copulationem, quam contra ecclesiasticam regulam constat esse contractam, matrimonium non esse censemus.
quotes.context: The step beyond continence: a marriage contracted by a cleric in major orders is declared no marriage at all, and the couple must separate (canon 6 also strips such clerics of office and benefice). Marriages made before ordination are not touched. Latin from the published conciliar text (Tanner, Decrees of the Ecumenical Councils, vol. 1); the web page’s Latin has a copying slip later in the canon, outside the span quoted here. Denzinger’s Enchiridion prints other Lateran II canons but not this one.

source.edition: Second Lateran Council, canon 7 (1139), Latin with English (Tanner, Decrees of the Ecumenical Councils, vol. 1)

quotes.author: Augsburg Confession (Lutheran)
quotes.english: It is also evident that in the ancient Church priests were married men. For Paul says, 1 Tim. 3:2, that a bishop should be chosen who is the husband of one wife.
quotes.original: It is also evident that in the ancient Church priests were married men. For Paul says, 1 Tim. 3:2, that a bishop should be chosen who is the husband of one wife.
quotes.context: The Lutheran defence of married clergy, from Scripture and the ancient Church’s practice; the same article says priests in Germany were first forced into celibacy about four hundred years before, in the Gregorian reform age. Quoted in the published English text; the Confession was presented in 1530 in Latin and German.
